commands.details: Establishes the release content. Exactly two commits landed after the v0.16.0 release commit: 8beec2cc 'fix(tests): remove two recurring main-branch flakes at their root (#377)' and 1dc2976b 'feat(release): gate foundation releases on their published artifact set (#380)'. Nothing else is unaccounted for, so v0.16.1 is a well-scoped patch.

Confirms the candidate commit for the release. Remote main is 1dc2976b5ff05fa79427b407422cb4c7a16ffcc6, which is the squash-merge of PR #380. Local main was stale at 3fe572f3 until fetched; the local branch was fast-forwarded so the release candidate and the local view agree.

Verifies the precondition publish-foundation-release.mjs enforces hardest. 'Release Gate Summary: completed/success started=2026-10-12T05:38:18Z' on the candidate commit. release-gate.yml triggers on push to main, so this is satisfied without any extra step. Had it been missing or not successful, publishFoundationRelease would have thrown before writing anything.

Generates a v0.16.1 manifest through the real build-release-manifest.mjs (it does not shell out, so it runs here) and diffs its sharedPaths against both the ops lock and the committed v0.13.0 manifest. Result: manifest 52 (backend 4, frontend 46, docs 2); ops lock 52; v0.13.0 manifest 52; zero paths only in the new manifest and zero only in the lock. The consumer lock therefore needs only version, commit and checksums advanced - no path declaration rewrite.

Extracts the six assembly anchors out of the consumer's own scripts/business-overlay/rebuild-from-base.mjs (wireBusinessRegistries) and asserts each still appears exactly once in the v0.16.1 base tree. All six pass. This matters because v0.16.0 renamed Go packages and moved frontend/src/modules/system/*, which is exactly the class of change that breaks an anchor and makes rebuild-from-base throw 'Base assembly contract changed'. Note the first attempt at this check under-reported (4 of 6) because two anchors are double-quoted in the source; the script was corrected to parse both quote styles before trusting the result.

commands.command: node -e "const {spawnSync}=require('node:child_process'); for (const c of ['git','gh','tar','node','echo']) { const r=spawnSync(c,['--version'],{encoding:'utf8'}); console.log(c, r.status, r.error && r.error.code); }"
commands.details: Establishes the binding constraint of this task. Every subprocess returns status=null with error.code=EBUSY: git, gh, tar, node and echo alike. Re-run with the sandbox disabled and the result is identical, so this is a host limitation rather than sandbox policy. Consequences: build-release-bundle.mjs (git rev-parse / git diff / git ls-files / git archive / tar) and publish-foundation-release.mjs (git, tar, gh) cannot run here, and neither can the consumer's rebuild-from-base.mjs. Hence the release is cut by a CI workflow.

Confirms the release can be built in CI without tripping publish's clean-worktree precondition. '.gitignore:68:releases/*/ releases/pantheon-base-v0.16.1/' - so the generated releases/<version>/ directory is ignored, and dist/ is ignored outright. Only releases/pantheon-base-v0.13.0/ is deliberately un-ignored. Had releases/<version>/ been tracked, ensureCleanWorktree would have failed after cut and publish could never have run.

commands.details: FIRST DISPATCH FAILED, after 7 seconds, at the Validate inputs step (run 38217014119): 'Missing or empty .harness/evidence/2026-10-12-v0161-release-cut/notes/release-notes.md'. The file is committed and present in the tree; the defect is step order. Validate inputs was the job's first step and ran before Checkout default branch, so it inspected an empty runner workspace. The check itself is right - it exists to fail fast on a bad notes_dir - but it cannot run before the tree is on disk. Nothing immutable was created: the failure happened before the tag, the release and any upload.

Validates the fix. Validate inputs now runs immediately after Checkout default branch and before Setup Node, so it still fails fast but with the tree present. The script asserts the ordering explicitly - Checkout at index 0 precedes Validate inputs at index 1 - rather than only re-checking YAML validity, because the original validation checked structure, SHA pins and the S7630 injection surface but never step order, which is exactly why this reached a hosted run. Also re-confirms: parses as YAML, workflow_dispatch only, both uses: entries SHA-pinned, workflow-level permissions contents: read with contents: write scoped to the single cut job, and no run block interpolates ${{ inputs.* }} or ${{ github.event.* }}.

commands.details: Run 38217942363, success in 17s. 'Releasing pantheon-base-v0.16.1 from c83f8e4c865b19ecd5351ecefac4106ec416e0bc'; then '[ok] local bundle pantheon-base-v0.16.1: foundation-release-pantheon-base-v0.16.1.tgz, repo.tar', which is the four-asset contract satisfied including both .sha256 sidecars; then publish invoked with --dry-run, emitting the planned operations create-tag, push-tag, create-github-release and upload-github-release-assets without executing them. This is the first time the cut/publish chain has ever run end to end in this repository - the scripts had only ever been covered by unit tests of themselves. It also confirms the release content is buildable from c83f8e4c while the runner's worktree sits at the newer main HEAD, which is what the baseCommit-versus-worktree check was designed to allow when the difference is not a sharedPath.

commands.command: gh workflow run foundation-release-cut.yml --ref main -f release_version=pantheon-base-v0.16.1 -f release_line=release/0.16 -f notes_dir=.harness/evidence/2026-10-12-v0161-release-cut/notes -f base_commit=c83f8e4c865b19ecd5351ecefac4106ec416e0bc -f dry_run=false
commands.details: SECOND HOSTED FAILURE, run 38218036804, 20s, at the Publish release step: 'git tag -a pantheon-base-v0.16.1 failed: Committer identity unknown ... fatal: empty ident name (for <runner@...>) not allowed'. The dry run never reaches createAnnotatedTag - it returns before the operations are executed - so this failure mode is structurally invisible to a dry run, which is the whole reason the real dispatch is a separate, non-redundant step. Root cause: actions/checkout with persist-credentials false sets no git identity, and the ubuntu-latest runner has no global one, but an annotated tag needs a committer. Verified afterwards that nothing immutable was created: gh api git/ref/tags/pantheon-base-v0.16.1 returns HTTP 404 and gh release view pantheon-base-v0.16.1 returns 'release not found'; the only v0.16 tag on the remote is pantheon-base-v0.16.0.

Validator extended for the second failure class and re-run. It now asserts, in addition to the previous checks, that some step configures a git committer identity, that that step precedes Publish release, that both 'git config user.name' and 'git config user.email' appear in a run block, and that the identity is github-actions[bot] with the GitHub noreply address rather than a personal one. Result: Checkout index 0 precedes Validate inputs index 1; identity step index 3 precedes Publish release index 7; identity is github-actions[bot]. The general lesson now recorded is that both hosted failures were environment-and-ordering assumptions that structural review could not see, and that each one is now pinned by an explicit assertion instead of a comment.

commands.command: gh workflow run foundation-release-cut.yml ... -f dry_run=false (three dispatches: 39350509094, 39351236715, 39351991489)
commands.details: All three hosted real cuts failed before creating anything immutable, each at a different environment boundary. 39350509094: 'refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow .github/workflows/foundation-release-cut.yml without `workflows` permission' at the tag push - the release candidate is the commit that adds that workflow, and `workflows` cannot be granted to GITHUB_TOKEN. 39351236715: after PR #388 moved tag creation to the Git database API, 'Resource not accessible by integration' (403), because this repository's default_workflow_permissions is read. 39351991489: after PR #389 reduced the workflow to a read-only ls-remote precheck plus fetch, the tag check passed but `gh release create` returned the same 403. Conclusion: no workflow step in this repository can write through the API with GITHUB_TOKEN, so publishing requires a token with contents:write. Nothing was tagged, released or uploaded by any of the three runs.

Final read-back after publishing: four assets - foundation-release-pantheon-base-v0.16.1.tgz (18500303 bytes), .tgz.sha256 (111), repo.tar (31477760), repo.tar.sha256 (75) - on a non-draft, non-prerelease release named v0.16.1 at tag pantheon-base-v0.16.1. For contrast the same command returns four names for v0.13.0 and nothing at all for v0.14.0/v0.15.0/v0.16.0.

This is a real defect in the workflow, not in the release content: base_commit was accepted as an input but never honoured by the checkout.

Creates the GitHub release and uploads the four assets with the maintainer credential. No tag or ref was modified.
Read-back confirms the four assets on a published (non-draft, non-prerelease) release.
Foundation Release Verify fired on release:published and passed, so the asset set the gate exists to protect is confirmed by CI rather than by the publisher's own claim.

runtimeGap: Two environment facts shaped this release. First, the preparing host could not spawn subprocesses on 2026-10-12 (spawnSync EBUSY for git/gh/tar), which is why the cut was rebuilt as a dispatch-only workflow; that limitation was gone by 2026-10-20, when the same canonical scripts ran locally in a detached worktree. Second, and decisively, no workflow step can write through the GitHub API in this repository: git push of a tag is refused for GitHub Apps without `workflows` permission (the candidate commit adds the workflow itself), and the Git database and release APIs return 403 'Resource not accessible by integration' because default_workflow_permissions is read. The tag was therefore created with a maintainer credential and the publish ran locally with the same credential. The workflow now verifies the tag read-only and remains the repeatable path for the bundle build and asset verification; fully unattended publishing needs a PAT secret with contents:write, which is a maintainer authorisation decision and is recorded as a known gap.
knownGaps: CI cannot publish in this repository without a token that has contents:write. Three hosted attempts (39350509094, 39351236715, 39351991489) each failed at a different wall - App `workflows` permission on tag push, then 403 on the Git database API, then 403 on release creation - so v0.16.1 was published locally with a maintainer credential. Closing this needs a PAT stored as a repository secret; that is an authorisation decision, not an engineering one.

The publish path exercised in production is therefore the local script invocation, not the workflow's publish step. The workflow's cut, asset-verification and tag-verification steps are proven green (runs 39350459932 and 39351991489); only its create-release/upload steps remain unproven in CI.

The consumer lock in pantheon-ops still points at pantheon-base-v0.13.0. Advancing it to v0.16.1, with the checksums read from the published release, is a separate consumer-repository change and was explicitly out of scope.

The consumer rebuild (npm run rebuild:from-base) has still not been run against v0.16.1. The six overlay anchors resolve exactly once in the candidate tree, but the first real assembly remains the authoritative verification of consumption.
Neither Foundation Release Cut nor Foundation Release Verify is a required check. Until a maintainer adds them to branch protection, a broken release goes red without blocking the next merge.
